facts.summary: EPA partially deleted the Townsend Saw Chain Co. Superfund Site in Pontiac from the National Priorities List in FY2019; EPA release dated October 29, 2019.
facts.quote: Townsend Saw Chain Co. Superfund Site in Pontiac, S.C.

facts.summary: EPA reuse snapshot reports that 35.5 of the original 50 acres were sold for commercial development; Centerline Development, LLC owns the remaining 14.5 acres. Undated snapshot.
facts.authority: U.S. EPA Superfund Redevelopment reuse snapshot (South Carolina)
facts.reference: Superfund Sites in Reuse in South Carolina
facts.quote: Of the original 50 acres, 35.5 acres of the site have been sold for commercial development.

gaps: Acreage conflicts across sources: 2 acres (1988 proposal narrative in a search snippet), 50 acres (EPA reuse snapshot), 400 acres (the 2019 partial deletion, per a search snippet). Not resolved; the 50-acre figure is the one recorded as a quote.
Richland County Property Search results and Register of Deeds records were not retrieved; no parcel, deed, lien or tax record was checked for this site.
The Register of Deeds portal link is referenced on the county assessor page but its URL was not given there and was not recorded.
EPA Federal Register notice 2019-20345 returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool, so the deletion text was taken from the EPA release only.
EPA CUMULIS site profile (ID 0403363, named in a search snippet) was not opened.

sites.name: CAROLAWN, INC.

facts.summary: EPA reuse snapshot describes Carolawn as a 60-acre Superfund site in Fort Lawn, South Carolina. Acreage is not consistent across sources (see gaps).
facts.authority: U.S. EPA Superfund Redevelopment reuse snapshot (South Carolina)
facts.reference: Superfund Sites in Reuse in South Carolina
facts.quote: The 60-acre Carolawn, Inc. Superfund site is located in Fort Lawn, South Carolina.

gaps: Chester County Assessor page (chestercountysc.gov/government/assessor) returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool. No Chester County assessor, GIS, treasurer or register of deeds portal was verified or recorded.
Acreage conflicts: one search summary says a 3-acre waste storage and disposal facility near Fishing Creek; EPA reuse snapshot says 60 acres. Only the 60-acre sentence is recorded.

The EPA reuse snapshot says Circle S Ranch acquired part of the site and a neighboring parcel and built a turkey feed mill (reported as 1996). I only retrieved a paraphrase of the acquisition sentence, so it is not recorded as a fact.
The 1989 and 1995 EPA decision documents and the 2010 CERCLA cost-payment agreement (CERCLA-04-2010-3753) appeared only in search snippets. No verbatim quote was retrieved, so they are not recorded.
Street address 5093 Morrison Road appears only in a search snippet of EPA settlement documents, not in an opened page.
No deed, lien, tax-delinquency or permit records were retrieved.

sites.name: HENRY'S KNOB

facts.summary: EPA release dated August 1, 2017 describes the 185-acre Henry's Knob Site at Henry Knob Road and State Highway 55 in Clover Township, York County.
facts.reference: EPA public meeting announcement for Henry's Knob former mine site
facts.quote: The 185-acre Henry’s Knob Site is located at the corner of Henry Knob Road and State Highway 55

facts.summary: The site was an open pit kyanite mine that operated from 1947 to 1970 (no month given).
facts.reference: EPA public meeting announcement for Henry's Knob former mine site
facts.quote: The Henry’s Knob Site was an open pit kyanite mine that operated from 1947 to 1970.

facts.summary: A proposed consent decree, published March 24, 2026 with a 30-day comment period, would have ABB, Inc. pay over $471,000 toward past cleanup costs and future expenses at the site.
facts.authority: Federal Register notice 2026-05674 (proposed consent decree), as reproduced on policyrisk.com
facts.quote: ABB will pay over $471,000 for past cleanup costs and cover future expenses while carrying out important cleanup work.

gaps: The Federal Register original (public-inspection.federalregister.gov/2026-05674.pdf) returned unreadable binary to the fetch tool; the consent decree facts rely on the policyrisk.com reproduction of the notice.

No York County portal was verified. The York County GIS page (yorkcountygov.com/234/GIS) redirects to yorkcountysc.gov, which returned HTTP 403. The One Map Reports parcel lookup it names was not opened.
No parcel id, owner or deed record was retrieved. The atlas owner is null.
A search snippet says the site has been privately owned since York County sold it in 1982; that is not recorded because no verbatim quote was retrieved.
Groundwater and well-count claims (about 450 homes; nearly 50 wells) came from a children's encyclopedia site and a TV headline and conflict with each other. Not recorded.

portals.note: Names the assessor (Molly Hartup) and links to the state TPAD property search (assessment.cot.tn.gov/TPAD), which returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool, and to a county GIS page (roanecountytn.gov/gis/) that was not opened.

portals.name: Anderson County property appraisal link (state assessment selector)
portals.note: The county page links 'See my Property Appraisal' to a Tennessee state assessment selector (assessment.cot.tn.gov/RE_Assessment). That linked page returned a hostname/certificate error to the fetch tool and was not opened.

facts.summary: EM says it has transferred more than 2,500 acres for private-sector reuse (undated page).
facts.authority: U.S. DOE Office of Environmental Management
facts.quote: EM has transferred more than 2,500 acres for private-sector reuse.

facts.summary: EPA and DOE confirmed that more than 16,000 acres of the broader Oak Ridge Reservation need no environmental cleanup.
facts.authority: U.S. DOE Office of Environmental Management / U.S. EPA
facts.quote: In December 2025, EPA and DOE confirmed that more than 16,000 acres of the broader Oak Ridge Reservation

facts.summary: DOE's Office of Environmental Management issued a Request for Proposals on September 30, 2025 seeking private partners to build and power AI data centers at the Oak Ridge Reservation.
facts.authority: U.S. DOE Office of Environmental Management
facts.quote: seeking private-sector partners to build and power AI data centers at the Oak Ridge Reservation

gaps: Oak Ridge is a federal reservation that spans Roane and Anderson counties. The atlas record has county null and no parcel id. No county parcel record was found for a federal tract, and whether federal tracts appear in county assessor rolls was not verified.
The Tennessee state property search (TPAD) returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool, so no parcel search was run.

Transfers reported only in search snippets are not recorded: 365 acres to CROET (February 2024), a 25-acre transfer to CROET (year unknown) and a 'largest transfer to date' of more than 700 acres (year unknown). No verbatim quote was retrieved for them.
No deed, lien, tax-delinquency or permit records were retrieved. Register of Deeds portals were not identified for either county.
